searchText: on smartcontracts that we store our money, like staking or L2, what procedure assures that only us and nobody else is able to withdraw our money? blockchain-wise, is it possible to know how much money each address has staked on the sc? same thing regarding some games that require us to transfer our NFT to their smartcontract so we can play with them, is there risk of somebody else stealing our NFT, or the smartcontract denying sending them back when we ask? staking and L2s are very different beasts for L2s the smart contract enforces it but the smart contract is enforced by the consensus protocol I mean transfer resources to sc then borrow it back I'm not sure what you're asking then somebody lent 5 NFT to a game sc, how can we be sure that these NFT won't be stolen and the sc will deliver them back when requested? you can't, generally you would have to know how the smart contract works we must read its source? then the rules for getting sole ownership of the NFT back are dependent on the rules described by the smart contract so yes so the owner of the sc can change it and steal all resources stored on it? smart contracts don't have owners smart contracts once deployed are immutable but you can write a smart contract that allows certain accounts to modify its behavior, potentially by replacing its implementation I thought new versions could be deployed what happens if a sc has some bug? then you need to design the smart contract in such a way that the implementation can be swapped out in the future how this is decided is dependent on the smart contract you can have a governance token system where a user can propose an update and token holders vote on whether or not to accept it but *all* of that is visible on-chain it is possible to *know* with certainty how a contract will behave in the future and how is this swap/update done? it depends look up the "proxy contract pattern" updatable behavior is something that must be opted into when developing the contract system initially, by default contracts are immutable and cannot not modify their behavior interesting so we must trust the sc to lend resources to it but we can read it and see what it does with these resources? yes you don't *have* to *trust* anything, you can read the code if there's a mechanism that allows a certain account to swap out the behavior without any delay then that's a red flag but if it *is* possible to swap out the behavior, it is possible to design these updatable systems in a way that users will have a grace period before an update can be applied what is a standard grace period? and im assuming in blocks right there is no standard, it's entirely dependent on the situation if it's something users are very involved with then that could be on the order of a day, for something more involved like a game that could be on the order of weeks/months if it's something like a game then it might be worthwhile to issue some governance token so users have to vote to accept an update, or vote to have an update applied sooner, but this could lead to bad incentives so if a bug is found and no block behavior exists then it can be exploited and nobody is able to stop it? yup which *is* a liability but it's also a strength, because it means that service providers can't just *decide* to change the rules on you Hopefully this is a decent place for this. Is there any merit to the daggers that are thrown by Cardano folks about Casper? Specifically that it isn't mathematically proven. Those daggers were thrown in video a while ago so maybe that has changed. Have no clue about Cardano nor any daggers, also don't know what lack of proof they refer to. What ultimately got implemented in Ethereum is very different than the original Casper paper, but the Casper paper in particular contains a couple of theorems : Theorem 1 proving accountable safety and theorem 2 proving plausible liveness, that can be read by any highschool student. If they claim those two are wrong or not proved, then I'd suspect anything else they say <@585239806007574538> Also worth noting that the phase0 beacon chain spec has been formally verified.
